titles: How Long Is ALL the DNA in Your Body? 🤯
Your DNA Unrolled Goes Past Pluto
Unroll Every Strand of Your DNA: How Far Does It Reach?
description: If you unrolled the DNA from every cell in your body and laid it end to end, how far would it reach? 🧬
About 74 billion km: past the Sun, past every planet, past Pluto, and almost 3 times farther than Voyager 1. Even light would need about 3 days to cross it.
• One cell holds ~6.4 billion DNA base pairs (two copies of the genome) × 0.34 nm ≈ 2 m of DNA
• ~37 trillion cells in a human body
• That's ~1.8 million trips around the Earth (40,075 km)
• Light: 74 billion km ÷ 300,000 km/s ≈ 69 hours ≈ 3 days

Milestones on the way (average distance from Earth): Moon 384,400 km, Sun 150 million km, Mars ~225 million km, Jupiter ~780 million km, Saturn ~1.4 billion km, Uranus ~2.9 billion km, Neptune ~4.5 billion km, Pluto ~5.9 billion km.

The catch: this assumes every cell has a full copy. Red blood cells (most of your cells!) have no nucleus and no DNA. Count only the cells that have DNA and you get roughly 6-20 billion km (estimates vary): still past Pluto. All numbers are approximate.
So... do red blood cells count? 👇
